episodes.159140: An area of high pressure reorganized over the Texas Panhandle which set up moist southerly flow across New Mexico on July 25, 2021. Above normal atmospheric moisture values helped to set the stage for scattered to numerous thunderstorms across central and western New Mexico as this more traditional monsoon pattern developed. Thunderstorms developed early in the day over the high terrain areas, and combined with weak steering flow and training cells, Lincoln County received some of the highest rainfall totals this day with reports of 1.5 to 3 inches of rain. This lead to flash flooding in the Angus area where water threatened to enter some homes. Flash flooding was also reported in Jemez Springs where the Jemez River overfilled its banks.
episodes.159143: A line of thunderstorms produced gusty winds to gale force over the northern tip of the Chesapeake Bay during the late evening.
episodes.159167: July 26, 2021 was yet another active monsoon day across northern and central New Mexico. With an area of high pressure over northern Colorado, moist southeasterly flow continued across much of New Mexico which resulted in another round of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. Thunderstorms developed first over the high terrain areas before coverage increased across lower elevations. The combination of heavy rainfall and slow steering flow resulted in a few reports of flash flooding across central New Mexico. The most notable event occurred over the Ute Park burn scar where the Colfax County emergency manager relayed reports of damage to multiple roadways in the area as well as numerous residents stranded in their homes.
episodes.159197: A pair of fronts spawned two clusters of severe thunderstorms that produced localized considerable wind damage near Staunton, Virginia, Silver Spring, Maryland, and Washington, DC.
episodes.159201: A pair of fronts spawned two clusters of severe thunderstorms that produced localized considerable wind damage near Staunton, Virginia, Silver Spring, Maryland, and Washington, DC.
episodes.159202: A pair of fronts spawned two clusters of severe thunderstorms that produced localized considerable wind damage near Staunton, Virginia, Silver Spring, Maryland, and Washington, DC.
episodes.159206: Multiple clusters of thunderstorms produced gusty winds over the upper half of the tidal Potomac River and portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.159244: Thunderstorms repeatedly trained Southwestward across Morgan County, producing large swaths of rainfall amounts between 3 to 6 inches over 2-3 hours on the evening of the 25th.
episodes.159296: The combination of a warm and humid air mass and daytime heating caused isolated strong to severe thunderstorms to develop across central and northeast Wisconsin.
episodes.159304: The combination of a warm and humid air mass and daytime heating caused isolated strong to severe thunderstorms to develop across northeast Wisconsin which moved across the southern Bay of Green Bay and the Lake Michigan nearshore waters during the afternoon hours.
episodes.159441: A weakening thunderstorm produced gusty winds along the western coast of north Merritt Island.
episodes.159548: Respectable monsoon moisture pushed into the region this week with a large high centered over the Four Corners and Rockies.
episodes.159627: Abundant monsoon moisture remained in place across the Western Slope. As a result, another round of widespread showers and thunderstorms developed across the area with many storms producing heavy rain. This led to localized flash flooding and debris flows across portions of Mesa, Ouray and Gunnison counties.
episodes.159748: A weak surface low drifted northward offshore of the local Atlantic coast, with bands of locally heavy rainfall across the local area. Aloft, warm, stable conditions prevailed under a COL region with a daily record precipitable water at JAX of 2.54. The tropical airmass combined with weak storm motion and low level convergence produced locally heavy rainfall in training bands today, with pockets of 2-4.5 inches of rainfall east of Highway 301.
episodes.160102: A severe thunderstorm with strong wind gusts near 70 mph caused tree damage in Sedgwick and Butler counties during the afternoon hours of July 26th, 2021.
episodes.160246: Typical summertime pattern for South FL, with showers and scattered to an isolated storm along the east coast through the first half of the day - transitioning to the interior and southwest Florida with storms becoming more numerous and robust by the afternoon hours. Lightning was the main hazard, and unfortunately struck two people on a beach near Naples.
episodes.160519: An area of low pressure lifted a warm front into the Northland during the day on the 26th. Behind this warm front was a moist and unstable airmass and daytime heating led to the development of strong to severe storms over northern Minnesota that moved to the southeast during the evening hours. One of the first storms was a supercell that produced hail 3 inches in diameter. Later storms continued to produce hail and damage to trees as they moved across the region. The Grand Rapids area in particular was hit hard in this event with widespread tree damage across the city. The KDLH radar was inoperable for this event but a high level of service was maintained by utilizing the KMVX and KMPX radars and one minute GOES-16 satellite data.
episodes.160558: A strong thunderstorm briefly became severe over central Bennett County, producing wind gusts over 60 mph in the Martin area.
episodes.160559: A thunderstorm became severe for a period over eastern Mellette County and produced large hail over quarter size.
episodes.160692: Isolated severe thunderstorms formed during the afternoon, producing heavy impacts as the result of large hail, damaging wind gusts, and several tornadoes.
episodes.160906: Thunderstorms developed near an area of low pressure across central South Dakota during the afternoon of July 25th, quickly intensifying to severe limits. These storms produced, at times, large to significantly large hail as they tracked to the east and southeast. The hail caused structural, vehicle, and crop damage. One of the more prolific storms produced hail continuously over a 3-hour window of time, extending about 125 miles from Faulk to Codington counties. The hail was up to nearly 4 inches in diameter at one location along the way.
episodes.160907: Thunderstorms developed near a surface low pressure area in South Dakota and moved east into west central Minnesota. Quarter size hail was observed in and around Wheaton.
episodes.161003: A deep easterly flow started to bring better moisture into the region with storms developing over the Organ Mountains.  Recent heavy rain over the east slopes of the Organ Mountains resulted in flash flooding and additional rain from this storm caused additional mud slides across Highway 70.
episodes.161005: A broad upper ridge was over the southern half of the country and an upper low was over southern Arizona. Moisture and instability were present across West Texas. These conditions allowed for a thunderstorm to develop that produced strong winds in the Permian Basin.
episodes.161043: Heavy rain associated with thunderstorms led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.161098: Convection moved southward out of Kansas during the afternoon of the 25th and continued into the rest of Oklahoma during the evening. Numerous severe wind reports were received.
episodes.161099: Remnant outflow and a mesoscale convective vortex helped to initiate convection across central and northern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 26th, with isolated severe wind gusts reported.
episodes.161108: A strong cold front combined with shortwave energy pushed through the region during the afternoon of July 26th, 2021. Widespread showers and storms develop as a result of an unstable airmass supported by CAPE values of 2,000-4000 j/kg. This contributed to the storms producing damaging winds through much of the afternoon and into the overnight hours.
episodes.161109: A strong cold front combined with shortwave energy pushed through the region during the afternoon of July 26th, 2021. Widespread showers and storms develop as a result of an unstable airmass supported by CAPE values of 2,000-3000 j/kg. This contributed to the storms producing damaging winds through much of the afternoon and into the overnight hours.
episodes.161309: Thunderstorms formed along a convergence line over south central North Dakota. One storm became severe south of Crystal Springs in Kidder County, producing half-dollar size hail.
episodes.161333: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
episodes.161472: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.161473: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.161478: Monsoonal thunderstorm activity occurred across Southern California from July 22 to July 29, with a major easterly wave producing widespread convection on July 25 and 26. Numerous reports of heavy rain leading to flash flooding and debris flows were received as well as reports of lightning, hail and dust storm.
episodes.161509: This is a continuation of the July 17-21 Thunderstorms episode, which lasted ten days total.
episodes.161510: This is a continuation of the July 17-21 Thunderstorms episode, which lasted ten days total.
episodes.161549: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms and scattered storm clusters developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon into the early evening. Multiple strong to severe cells developed, producing brief damaging wind gusts, mainly across the Piedmont.
episodes.161553: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms and scattered storm clusters moved into the South Carolina Piedmont from western North Carolina during the late afternoon and early evening. One severe storm produced damaging wind gusts in the Lake Wylie area.
episodes.161554: An isolated thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Walworth County.
episodes.161576: A west to east oriented cold front dropped south through central Kentucky. This kicked off a few widely scattered thunderstorms that caused a houseboat, on Lake Cumberland, to roll onto its side and some area tree damage.
episodes.161676: Monsoon moisture which had been fueling thunderstorms over southern Nevada and northwest Arizona for days seeped west into southeast California, triggering several flash floods.
episodes.161685: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the morning hours on July 26. An isolated wind damage report was received as well as damage to a home from a lightning strike.
episodes.161690: A retrograding upper level low combined with anomalously high moisture levels led to showers and isolated thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall and numerous instances of considerable flash flooding across south-central Arizona on the 25th. The places that saw the heaviest rainfall amounts were areas that experienced heavy showers training over the same locations. Western portions of the Phoenix metro saw training showers with heavy rainfall occur, leading to widespread amounts of 1.5-2.5 with locally higher amounts of 3+. As a result, there were numerous reports of flash flooding, including multiple water rescues and numerous road closures due to flooding. Heavy rainfall also fell over multiple burn scars, leading to several instances of burn scar flash flooding. One of the burn scars that saw heavy rainfall was the Bush fire burn scar, which led to enhanced runoff and a rapid rise on Sycamore Creek. Several people were rescued after getting stuck in the increased flow in Sycamore Creek. No injuries were reported.
episodes.161779: A retrograding upper level low combined with highly anomalous moisture values allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop across southeast California and produce several instances of flash flooding along with isolated damaging wind gusts. Showers and thunderstorms began developing across southeast California late in the morning and into the afternoon on the 25th. Some thunderstorms became strong to severe, with one severe thunderstorm producing some damage in Joshua Tree National Park. Showers and thunderstorms continued through the rest of the day on the 25th with additional development again early in the morning on the 26th. No injuries were reported.
episodes.161889: A strong thunderstorm developed along a frontal boundary in the presence of 40 knots of deep-layer shear, which resulted in a briefly rotating storm producing marginally large hail.
episodes.161903: A cold front triggered a severe thunderstorm across Southeastern New York.
episodes.161949: Another active period across southern Colorado on this day, with showers and thunderstorms observed over much of the area. The eastern mountain and I-25 corridor interface was a location with more widespread development, especially along the Highway 50 corridor. In this area, heavy rainfall with flooding, large hail, and damaging winds were observed.
episodes.162203: Deep monsoon moisture remained over northern Arizona with strong thunderstorms across the area. An area of low pressure moving over the area from the east help form thunderstorm complexes that brought widespread moderate to heavy rain to northern Arizona.

Mesa County Sheriff's Office responded to a report of two hikers trapped by flash flood waters in Rough Canyon. When deputies arrived at the trailhead, it was discovered several other people were also unable to reach the parking lot due to rising floodwaters.  Storms in the area quickly turned what typically is a dried creek bed at the start of the trail into an unpassable rushing river. Rescue crews estimate it was about 15 feet wide and 3-5 feet deep. It took about 6 hours for the water to recede enough for rescuers to reach everyone. Four families, who started the day on a hike or UTV trail, were safely rescued.

Initial report of a tornado on Lower Red Lake, which moved onshore at Red Lake and tracked for less than one mile. The tornado lifted by 515 PM CDT. Damaging downburst winds, heavy rain, and large hail continued to track southeastward with this storm. Damage was reported to the Tribal College, as well as other homes and buildings in the area. A light pole was snapped and several signs were toppled. Several large trees were snapped.

Hail up to tennis ball sized, as well as downburst winds of near 70 mph impacted the areas between the Communities of Red Lake and Redby, as well as the Tribal lands immediately south and southeast of these Communities. Widespread shingle and roofing damage was evident, along with home and vehicle windows shattered. Several large tree limbs blown down and large trees snapped.

This tornado formed near the shore of Lower Red Lake and tracked to the southeast. It crossed MN HWY 1 near the intersection with BIA15 and penetrated deeply into a large evergreen and oak forest. Trees were snapped and debris was tangled, though most debris tracked with the southeast moving storm. The tornado appeared to have dissipated around 522 PM CDT, after crossing BIA18, roughly 6 miles ESE of Redby.

A few trees were reported down in the Daleville area due to thunderstorm winds.

Numerous trees and wires blew down in and near Silver Spring and Takoma Park. Damage was most focused and severe along Sligo Creek Parkway and along MD-320 Piney Branch Road between Sligo Creek and the DC line; trees blew into two houses in the 7400 and 7900 block of MD-320 Piney Branch Road with wires also down, and several trees a few feet in diameter were uprooted tearing down poles and wires blocking MD-320 Piney Creek Road between Sligo Avenue and Mississippi Avenue/Parkside Road for more than a day.||Several trees and large branches also blew down along I-495 Capital Beltway; a tree blew down onto I-495 Capital Beltway Inner Loop at Exit 31A/southbound MD-97 Georgia Avenue, a tree blew down on I-495 Capital Beltway Inner Loop between Exit 29/MD-193 University Boulevard and Exit 28B/westbound MD-650 New Hampshire Avenue, and a tree blew down on I-495 Capital Beltway Outer Loop just west of Exit 30/US-29 Colesville Road.||Elsewhere nearby, a large tree blew down onto a house taking down wires in the 8100 block of Flower Avenue, and a tree blew down on MD-410 East West Highway at Ellingson Drive. A few dozen other large branches and trees fell in the area, some onto wires and cars.
A photo was received of a power pole that was snapped in Wirt.
There were multiple trees down on power lines, mainly along and near Highway 127 North.
Several reports of tennis ball to baseball sized hail near Pennington in southern Moose Lake and in Brook Lake Townships from 605 PM CDT to 615 PM CDT. Photos and reports relayed via social media.

There were over 100 trees, branches and wires blown down throughout DC. Several of them were in the Queens Chapel, Avondale, University Heights and Brookland neighborhoods in Northeast DC, including a tree that blew down onto a house in the 1300 block of Webster Street Northeast.
Photos were received of damage to trees and docks around Side Lake.

There were over 100 trees, branches and wires blown down throughout DC. One of the hardest hit areas was in Northwest DC, where several dozen trees, limbs and wires blew down in the Petworth, Columbia Heights and Mount Pleasant neighborhoods; minor roof damage was observed at at least two apartment buildings in Petworth. The railing of a rooftop of one apartment building was torn off, with a large tree falling and crushing cars nearby. A section of parapet wall and roof decking blew off a second (vacant) apartment building in the 2900 block of Ontario Road Northwest. A large tree blew over (split at the trunk) and fell on and crushed a car near the intersection of Taylor Street Northwest and Kansas Avenue Northwest. A tree blew down onto Georgia Avenue Northwest near Taylor Street Northwest. Several 3 to 6 inch in diameter tree limbs blew down on 14th Street Northwest near Arkansas Avenue Northwest. A tree blew down in the 1200 block of Randolph Street Northwest.  A large tree blew down blocking portions of Quincy Street Northwest.
Photos and video were received of damage along the shore of Jessie Lake. A dock was overturned along with a boat lift. A pontoon boat that was on the boat lift was also overturned.

There were over 100 trees, branches and wires blown down throughout DC, including in the Adams Morgan, Shaw, and Edgewood neighborhoods in Northwest DC, where a few dozen trees, branches and wires blew down. A wind gust of 58 knots (67 MPH) was measured by a mesonet at Children's Hospital. A tree blew down near the intersection of 15th Street Northwest and S Street Northwest. Several large tree limbs blew down on 16th Street Northwest near Kalorama Road Northwest. A very large tree blew down onto a row house in the 600 block of Irving Street Northwest.
